questions.explanation: No. The B that is not C may lie outside A. The premises do not guarantee that any A is outside C. All A are B, but the B outside C may not include any A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The city should impose a fine on littering to keep the streets clean.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Fines are the only way to keep streets clean
options.B: The fine can deter littering and thereby help keep the streets clean
options.C: Littering is not a problem
options.D: All citizens will refuse to pay fines

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that the fine can deter littering and thereby help keep the streets clean. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense. The assumption need not be the only solution.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'Every student in the class submitted the assignment on time.' What can be inferred?

options.A: Some students submitted late
options.B: No student in the class submitted late
options.C: All students in the school submitted on time
options.D: The assignment was easy

questions.explanation: If every student in the class submitted on time, then no student in the class submitted late. The inference must not go beyond the passage (it does not say anything about the whole school or the difficulty of the assignment).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'Some of the books in the library are damaged.' What can be inferred?

options.A: All books in the library are damaged
options.B: At least one book in the library is damaged
options.C: No book in the library is damaged
options.D: Most books in the library are damaged

questions.explanation: 'Some of the books are damaged' means at least one book is damaged. It does not mean all or most are damaged, and it does not mean none are damaged.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A person exercises regularly. Event II: The person's fitness improves. What is the relationship?

options.A: Regular exercise is a plausible cause of improved fitness
options.B: Improved fitness causes regular exercise
options.C: The two events are unrelated
options.D: Improved fitness definitely and solely causes regular exercise

questions.explanation: Regular exercise is a plausible cause of improved fitness. The relationship is direct and plausible. However, other factors such as diet and genetics may also contribute.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A student studies regularly. Event II: The student scores well in the examination. What is the relationship?

options.A: Regular study is a plausible cause of good scores, though other factors may also contribute
options.B: Good scores cause regular study
options.C: The two events are unrelated
options.D: Good scores definitely and solely cause regular study

questions.explanation: Regular study is a plausible cause of good scores. However, other factors such as prior knowledge, teaching quality, and examination difficulty may also contribute.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a compound statement?

options.A: The examination begins at 10 a.m.
options.B: The sun rises in the east and the moon orbits the earth.
options.C: Please sit down.
options.D: What time is it?

questions.explanation: A compound statement is formed by combining two or more propositions using logical connectors. 'The sun rises in the east and the moon orbits the earth' combines two propositions with AND.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an argument from principle?

options.A: The policy should be adopted because it will reduce costs
options.B: The policy should be adopted because it upholds the principle of equality
options.C: The policy should be adopted because it is feasible
options.D: The policy should be adopted because many people support it

questions.explanation: An argument from principle supports or opposes an action by referring to a rule, right, duty, fairness, equality, or other normative principle. 'It upholds the principle of equality' is an argument from principle.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an argument from feasibility?

options.A: The policy should be adopted because it is fair
options.B: The policy should be adopted because the budget, staff, and infrastructure are available to implement it
options.C: The policy should be adopted because it will reduce costs
options.D: The policy should be adopted because it is popular

questions.explanation: An argument from feasibility evaluates whether a proposal can practically be implemented, considering resources, time, infrastructure, authority, and operational constraints. Availability of budget, staff, and infrastructure is a feasibility argument.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an argument from consequences?

options.A: The policy should be adopted because it is fair
options.B: The policy should be adopted because it will reduce unemployment and boost economic growth
options.C: The policy should be adopted because it is feasible
options.D: The policy should be adopted because it is popular

questions.explanation: An argument from consequences supports or opposes an action by explaining its likely benefits, harms, costs, or wider effects. Reducing unemployment and boosting growth are consequences.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. All A are C. Conclusion: Some B are C. Does it follow?

options.A: Yes; the A that exists (if any) is both B and C, so some B are C
options.B: No, because A may not exist
options.C: Only if all B are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. All A are B and All A are C. If any A exists, it is both B and C, so some B are C. Under the standard examination convention that assumes existence when universal statements are made about a class, the conclusion follows.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following best describes an implicit assumption?

options.A: An assumption that is directly written in the statement
options.B: An assumption that is not directly written but is required for the statement or argument to make sense
options.C: An assumption that is always false
options.D: An assumption that is a conclusion

questions.explanation: An implicit assumption is not directly written in the statement but is required or presupposed for the statement or argument to make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The train was delayed by two hours.' What can be inferred?

options.A: The train arrived two hours late
options.B: The train's scheduled time was two hours earlier than its actual time, assuming no other delays occurred
options.C: The train will never be on time
options.D: The train was cancelled

questions.explanation: If the train was delayed by two hours, its actual time was two hours later than its scheduled time, assuming no other delays occurred. The passage does not say the train will never be on time or that it was cancelled.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a particular statement?

options.A: All applicants must carry an identity card
options.B: Every student passed the examination
options.C: Some teachers are writers
options.D: Each member must pay the fee

questions.explanation: A particular statement makes a claim about at least one or some members of a group. 'Some teachers are writers' is a particular statement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a universal statement?

options.A: Some students passed
options.B: All applicants must carry an identity card
options.C: A few teachers are writers
options.D: At least one member attended

questions.explanation: A universal statement makes a claim about every member of a group. 'All applicants must carry an identity card' is a universal statement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: No A is B. Some C are A. Conclusion: Some C are not B. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; the C that is A cannot be B, because no A is B
options.C: Only if all C are A
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some C are A. No A is B. The C that is A cannot be B. Therefore, some C are not B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Is an argument strong merely because it uses emotional language?

options.A: Yes, emotional language makes an argument strong
options.B: No; emotional language should be ignored, and the argument must be evaluated on relevance, significance, and logical support
options.C: Yes, if the emotion is genuine
options.D: Only in advertisements

questions.explanation: Emotional language should be ignored. An argument must be evaluated on relevance, significance, and logical support. Emotional manipulation is a characteristic of weak arguments.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The number of students opting for science stream has declined over the past five years.' Which inference is best supported?

options.A: Science is no longer important
options.B: Fewer students are choosing the science stream now than five years ago
options.C: All students now prefer arts
options.D: The quality of science teaching has declined

questions.explanation: The passage states that the number of students opting for the science stream has declined over five years. The best-supported inference is that fewer students are choosing science now than five years ago. The other options go beyond the passage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A country increased its spending on education. Event II: Literacy rates improved over the next decade. What is the most careful conclusion?

options.A: The increased spending definitely caused the improvement
options.B: The increased spending may have contributed to the improvement, but other factors such as social changes, economic growth, or private initiatives could also explain it
options.C: The improvement in literacy caused the increased spending
options.D: The two events are unrelated

questions.explanation: The increased spending may have contributed to the improvement, but other factors such as social changes, economic growth, or private initiatives could also explain it. Causation requires additional evidence; correlation and sequence alone are not sufficient.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The company should advertise on social media to reach more customers.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Social media is the only way to reach customers
options.B: The target customers use social media and advertising there can reach them
options.C: All customers use social media
options.D: Advertising is always effective

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that the target customers use social media and that advertising there can reach them. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense. The assumption need not be the only way.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the negation of 'All students passed'?

options.A: All students failed
options.B: Some students did not pass
options.C: No student passed
options.D: Some students passed

questions.explanation: The negation of 'All students passed' is 'Some students did not pass'. These two statements are contradictory: they cannot both be true and cannot both be false.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the negation of 'Some students passed'?

options.A: All students passed
options.B: No student passed
options.C: Some students failed
options.D: All students failed

questions.explanation: The negation of 'Some students passed' is 'No student passed'. These two statements are contradictory: they cannot both be true and cannot both be false.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some B are C. Some C are D. Conclusion: Some A are D. Does it follow?

options.A: Yes, definitely
options.B: No; the chain of 'some' relationships does not guarantee any overlap between A and D
options.C: Yes, if all C are D
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. The 'some' relationships do not guarantee any overlap between A and D. The B that is C and the C that is D may not involve any A. Multiple 'some' statements do not produce a definite conclusion about A and D.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The library is open on all weekdays except public holidays.' What can be inferred about a public holiday that falls on a Wednesday?

options.A: The library is open
options.B: The library is closed
options.C: The library may or may not be open
options.D: The library is open only in the morning

questions.explanation: The passage states the library is open on all weekdays except public holidays. If a public holiday falls on a Wednesday, the library is closed. The inference follows directly from the passage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A person smokes regularly. Event II: The person develops a persistent cough. What is the relationship?

options.A: Smoking is a plausible cause of the cough, though other factors may also contribute
options.B: The cough causes smoking
options.C: The two events are unrelated
options.D: The cough definitely and solely causes smoking

questions.explanation: Smoking is a plausible cause of a persistent cough. However, other factors such as allergies, infections, or environmental conditions may also contribute. Causation requires additional evidence beyond sequence and plausibility.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a fact-based argument?

options.A: The policy is good because I like it
options.B: The policy is good because data show it reduced poverty by 10%
options.C: The policy is good because it sounds fair
options.D: The policy is good because my friend supports it

questions.explanation: A fact-based argument relies on verifiable information, evidence, data, or established conditions rather than merely personal preference. 'Data show it reduced poverty by 10%' is a fact-based argument.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an opinion-based argument?

options.A: The policy is good because data show it reduced poverty
options.B: The policy is good because it seems fair to me
options.C: The policy is good because it is feasible
options.D: The policy is good because it follows a legal rule

questions.explanation: An opinion-based argument expresses a personal judgment or preference. 'It seems fair to me' is an opinion-based argument. It can still be relevant but may provide weaker support than reliable evidence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. No B is C. Some D are C. Conclusion: Some D are not A. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; the D that is C cannot be B (since no B is C), and therefore cannot be A (since all A are B)
options.C: Only if all D are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some D are C. No B is C, so the D that is C cannot be B. All A are B, so anything that is not B cannot be A. Therefore, some D are not A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The school should provide free meals to all students to improve attendance.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Free meals are the only way to improve attendance
options.B: Providing free meals can influence attendance, and the school has the resources to provide them
options.C: All students are hungry
options.D: Attendance is not important

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that providing free meals can influence attendance and that the school has the resources to provide them. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense. The assumption need not be the only solution.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The new policy requires all employees to attend a training session. Ravi is an employee.' What can be inferred?

options.A: Ravi has already attended the training
options.B: Ravi is required to attend a training session
options.C: Ravi will refuse to attend the training
options.D: Ravi is not an employee

questions.explanation: The policy requires all employees to attend a training session. Ravi is an employee. Therefore, Ravi is required to attend a training session. This is a direct inference.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A company introduced a new software system. Event II: Employee productivity increased. What is the most careful conclusion?

options.A: The software definitely caused the productivity increase
options.B: The software may have contributed to the productivity increase, but other factors such as training, management changes, or employee motivation could also explain it
options.C: The productivity increase caused the software introduction
options.D: The two events are unrelated

questions.explanation: The software may have contributed to the productivity increase, but other factors such as training, management changes, or employee motivation could also explain it. Causation requires additional evidence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government invest in renewable energy? Argument: Yes, because renewable energy reduces dependence on fossil fuels and lowers long-term energy costs. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides significant reasons directly supporting the proposal
options.C: No, because renewable energy is expensive
options.D: Yes, because many people support it

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects renewable energy to reduced fossil fuel dependence and lower long-term costs, both directly related to the proposal. It provides reasons supporting the action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is logically equivalent to 'No A is B'?

options.A: All A are B
options.B: No B is A
options.C: Some A are B
options.D: Some A are not B

questions.explanation: 'No A is B' can be validly converted to 'No B is A' because the two groups are mutually exclusive. This is a valid conversion.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some C are not B. Conclusion: Some C are not A. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; the C that is not B cannot be A, because all A are inside B
options.C: Only if some C are A
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. All A are B. Some C are not B. The C that lies outside B cannot be A, because every A is inside B. Therefore, some C are not A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes an assumption from a conclusion?

options.A: An assumption is stated, while a conclusion is unstated
options.B: An assumption is an unstated supporting idea on which reasoning depends, while a conclusion is the claim that the reasoning attempts to establish
options.C: An assumption is always false, while a conclusion is always true
options.D: They are the same

questions.explanation: An assumption is an unstated supporting idea on which the reasoning depends. A conclusion is the claim that the reasoning attempts to establish.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a weak argument based on an incorrect assumption?

options.A: The road should be repaired because potholes have caused accidents
options.B: The road should be repaired because all roads in the country are in poor condition
options.C: The road should be repaired because it is used by many commuters
options.D: The road should be repaired because it connects two important towns

questions.explanation: The argument 'all roads in the country are in poor condition' is based on an unsupported generalisation and does not directly address the need to repair this particular road. It is a weak argument based on an incorrect or unsupported assumption.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'A study found that people who read books regularly tend to live longer than those who do not.' Which inference is best supported?

options.A: Reading books definitely causes longer life
options.B: There is an association between regular book reading and longer life, but other factors may explain the difference
options.C: People who do not read books will die young
options.D: Reading books is the only factor in longevity

questions.explanation: The passage reports an association (correlation). It does not prove causation. Other factors such as education, income, lifestyle, and health behaviours may explain the difference. The cautious inference is that an association exists.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A city planted more trees along its roads. Event II: Air quality in those areas improved. What is the most careful conclusion?

options.A: The trees definitely caused the improvement
options.B: The trees may have contributed to the improvement, but other factors such as reduced traffic or weather changes could also explain it
options.C: The improvement in air quality caused the trees to be planted
options.D: The two events are unrelated

questions.explanation: The trees may have contributed to the improvement, but other factors such as reduced traffic or weather changes could also explain it. Causation requires additional evidence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct negation of 'Some A are B'?

options.A: All A are B
options.B: No A is B
options.C: Some A are not B
options.D: All A are not B

questions.explanation: The negation of 'Some A are B' is 'No A is B'. These two statements are contradictory: they cannot both be true and cannot both be false.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some B are not C. Conclusion: Some A are not C. Does it follow?

options.A: No; the B that is not C may lie outside A
options.B: Yes, definitely
options.C: Only if all B are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. The B that is not C may lie outside A. The premises do not guarantee that any A is outside C. All A are B, but the B outside C may not include any A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The government should increase funding for public libraries to promote reading habits.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Public libraries are the only way to promote reading
options.B: Increased funding for public libraries can help promote reading habits
options.C: Reading habits are not important
options.D: All citizens use public libraries

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that increased funding for public libraries can help promote reading habits. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense. The assumption need not be the only way.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government provide free public transport? Argument: Yes, because it would reduce traffic congestion and pollution. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides significant reasons directly supporting the proposal
options.C: No, because free transport is impossible
options.D: Yes, because everyone likes free things

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects free public transport to reduced traffic congestion and pollution, both directly related to the proposal. It provides reasons supporting the action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The company's revenue has grown every year for the past five years.' What can be inferred about the company's revenue this year compared to five years ago?

options.A: It is lower now
options.B: It is higher now
options.C: It is the same
options.D: It cannot be determined

questions.explanation: If revenue has grown every year for five years, it is higher now than five years ago. This is a direct inference from the passage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates the difference between correlation and causation?

options.A: Smoking causes lung cancer
options.B: Ice cream sales and drowning incidents both increase in summer, but ice cream does not cause drowning
options.C: Exercise improves fitness
options.D: Rain causes the ground to become wet

questions.explanation: Ice cream sales and drowning incidents both increase in summer due to a confounding factor (hot weather), but ice cream does not cause drowning. This illustrates that correlation does not prove causation.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a simple statement?

options.A: The examination begins at 10 a.m. and ends at 1 p.m.
options.B: The examination begins at 10 a.m.
options.C: The examination is easy or difficult
options.D: If the examination is easy, students pass

questions.explanation: A simple statement expresses one proposition without joining it to another proposition through a logical connector. 'The examination begins at 10 a.m.' is a simple statement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. No B is C. Some C are D. Conclusion: Some D are not A. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; the D that is C cannot be B (since no B is C), and therefore cannot be A (since all A are B)
options.C: Only if all D are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some C are D. No B is C, so the C that is D cannot be B. All A are B, so anything that is not B cannot be A. Therefore, some D are not A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The company should hire more salespeople to increase revenue.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Salespeople are the only way to increase revenue
options.B: Hiring more salespeople can contribute to increased revenue
options.C: The company has no revenue problems
options.D: All salespeople are effective

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that hiring more salespeople can contribute to increased revenue. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense. The assumption need not be the only way.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a strong argument?

options.A: The policy should be adopted because my friend supports it
options.B: The policy should be adopted because it will reduce pollution and improve public health
options.C: The policy should be adopted because it is popular on social media
options.D: The policy should be adopted because the person proposing it is famous

questions.explanation: A strong argument is relevant to the issue, logically connected to the conclusion, and supported by credible or significant reasons. 'It will reduce pollution and improve public health' provides significant, relevant reasons.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The city's population has grown by 20% in the last decade, and the number of vehicles has grown by 35%.' What can be inferred about traffic congestion?

options.A: Traffic congestion has definitely worsened
options.B: The growth in population and vehicles may have contributed to increased traffic congestion, though the passage does not directly state congestion levels
options.C: Traffic congestion has improved
options.D: Population growth caused vehicle growth

questions.explanation: The passage states growth in population and vehicles but does not directly state congestion levels. The best-supported inference is that these growth factors may have contributed to increased traffic congestion. Other factors could also affect congestion.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A student starts using a new study technique. Event II: The student's exam scores improve. Which of the following would weaken the claim that the technique caused the improvement?

options.A: The student used the technique consistently
options.B: The student also started attending extra coaching classes at the same time
options.C: The student found the technique easy to use
options.D: The technique is recommended by teachers

questions.explanation: If the student also started attending extra coaching classes at the same time, this is a confounding factor that could explain the improvement. It weakens the claim that the study technique alone caused the improvement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In logic, 'P or Q' is false only when:

options.A: P is true and Q is true
options.B: P is false and Q is false
options.C: P is true and Q is false
options.D: P is false and Q is true

questions.explanation: Logical OR is inclusive: 'P or Q' is true when at least one of P or Q is true, including when both are true. It is false only when both P and Q are false.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some C are B. Conclusion: Some C are A. Does it follow?

options.A: Yes, definitely
options.B: No; the C that is B may not be A, since all A are B does not mean all B are A
options.C: Yes, if all C are B
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. Some C are B, but the C that is B may not be A. 'All A are B' does not mean 'All B are A'. The overlap between C and B may lie outside A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The government should provide subsidies to farmers to increase agricultural production.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Subsidies are the only way to increase production
options.B: Subsidies can influence farmers' decisions and thereby increase agricultural production
options.C: Farmers do not need any support
options.D: All farmers will use subsidies effectively

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that subsidies can influence farmers' decisions and thereby increase agricultural production. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government ban single-use plastics? Argument: Yes, because single-use plastics contribute significantly to environmental pollution. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides a significant environmental reason directly supporting the ban
options.C: No, because plastics are useful
options.D: Yes, because everyone supports the ban

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects single-use plastics to environmental pollution, a concern directly related to the proposal. It provides a reason supporting the ban.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'All the windows in the building were closed. The room was still cold.' What can be inferred?

options.A: The heating system may not have been working or the insulation may be poor
options.B: The windows were open
options.C: The building has no heating system
options.D: The room was warm

questions.explanation: If all windows were closed and the room was still cold, possible explanations include a non-working heating system or poor insulation. The inference must be supported by the passage and not go beyond what is reasonable.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a direct cause?

options.A: A prolonged drought leading to crop failure through several intermediate steps
options.B: A spark igniting a fire
options.C: Poor forest management years earlier contributing to a fire
options.D: Climate change affecting weather patterns

questions.explanation: A direct cause has an immediate causal connection with the effect, without a substantial chain of intermediate events. A spark igniting a fire is a direct cause.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of 'Only A are B'?

options.A: All A are B
options.B: All B are A
options.C: Some A are B
options.D: No A is B

questions.explanation: In 'Only A are B', every B is A; it does not state that every A is B. For example, 'Only graduates are eligible' means all eligible persons are graduates.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: Some A are B. All B are C. No C is D. Conclusion: Some A are not D. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; the A that is B is also C, and no C is D, so that A is not D
options.C: Only if all A are B
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some A are B. All B are C, so the A that is B is also C. No C is D, so that A is not D. Therefore, some A are not D.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the best description of a hidden assumption?

options.A: An assumption that is clearly stated in the argument
options.B: An unstated belief connecting the evidence to the conclusion, possibly concerning reliability of information, relevance of evidence, or expected effect of an action
options.C: A conclusion drawn from the premises
options.D: A fact presented as established information

questions.explanation: A hidden assumption is an unstated belief connecting the evidence to the conclusion. It may concern the reliability of information, the relevance of evidence, or the expected effect of an action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following statements about strong arguments is correct?

options.A: An argument is strong if it is long and detailed
options.B: An argument is strong if it is relevant, significant, logical, and adequately supported
options.C: An argument is strong if it is popular
options.D: An argument is strong if it uses emotional language

questions.explanation: A strong argument is relevant to the issue, logically connected to the conclusion, and supported by credible or significant reasons. It directly addresses the question being asked.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The store offers a discount on all items on weekends.' What can be inferred about a purchase made on a Sunday?

options.A: The purchase will receive the discount
options.B: The purchase may or may not receive the discount depending on whether Sunday is considered a weekend
options.C: The purchase will not receive the discount
options.D: The store is closed on Sunday

questions.explanation: Sunday is generally considered part of the weekend, so the purchase will likely receive the discount. However, the passage does not explicitly define 'weekend'. The safest inference is that the discount applies if Sunday is considered a weekend.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A person consumes excessive sugar. Event II: The person develops dental problems. What is the relationship?

options.A: Excessive sugar consumption is a plausible cause of dental problems
options.B: Dental problems cause excessive sugar consumption
options.C: The two events are unrelated
options.D: Dental problems definitely and solely cause sugar consumption

questions.explanation: Excessive sugar consumption is a plausible cause of dental problems. However, other factors such as oral hygiene and genetics may also contribute.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a contradictory pair?

options.A: 'All students passed' and 'No student passed'
options.B: 'All students passed' and 'Some students did not pass'
options.C: 'Some students passed' and 'Some students failed'
options.D: 'All students passed' and 'All students passed'

questions.explanation: Two statements are contradictory when they cannot both be true and cannot both be false. 'All students passed' and 'Some students did not pass' are contradictory when they refer to the same group and examination.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. No B is C. Conclusion: No A is C. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; A is inside B, and B has no overlap with C, so A has no overlap with C
options.C: Only if some A are B
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. All A are inside B, and no B is C. Therefore, no A can be C. This is a valid chain of reasoning.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The hospital should hire more nurses to improve patient care.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Nurses are the only factor in patient care
options.B: Hiring more nurses can contribute to improved patient care
options.C: The hospital has no nurses
options.D: All patients are dissatisfied

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that hiring more nurses can contribute to improved patient care. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government build more highways? Argument: Yes, because better roads reduce travel time. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides a significant reason directly supporting the proposal
options.C: No, because highways are expensive
options.D: Yes, because everyone likes highways

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects better roads to reduced travel time, which is directly related to the proposal. It provides a reason supporting the action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The new employee completed all assigned tasks ahead of schedule.' What can be inferred?

options.A: The employee is efficient or works quickly
options.B: The employee will be promoted
options.C: The employee did not complete the tasks
options.D: The employee is not competent

questions.explanation: If the employee completed all assigned tasks ahead of schedule, it can be inferred that the employee is efficient or works quickly. The passage does not state anything about promotion or competence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A business lowers its prices. Event II: Sales increase. What is the most careful conclusion?

options.A: Lower prices definitely caused the sales increase
options.B: Lower prices may have contributed to the sales increase, but other factors such as advertising, seasonality, or competitor actions could also explain it
options.C: The sales increase caused the price reduction
options.D: The two events are unrelated

questions.explanation: Lower prices may have contributed to the sales increase, but other factors such as advertising, seasonality, or competitor actions could also explain it. Causation requires additional evidence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a consistent set of statements?

options.A: 'All students passed' and 'Some students failed'
options.B: 'All students passed' and 'No student failed'
options.C: 'No student passed' and 'Some students passed'
options.D: 'All A are B' and 'No A is B'

questions.explanation: 'All students passed' and 'No student failed' can both be true together. Options A, C, and D are inconsistent because they contain contradictory pairs.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: Some A are B. All B are C. Conclusion: Some A are C. Does it follow?

options.A: Yes; the A that is B is also C
options.B: No; the A that is B may not be C
options.C: Only if all A are B
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some A are B. All B are C. The A that is B is also C. Therefore, some A are C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The government should launch a campaign to encourage citizens to save water.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Campaigns are the only way to save water
options.B: A campaign can influence citizens' behaviour and thereby encourage water conservation
options.C: Water is not scarce
options.D: All citizens waste water

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that a campaign can influence citizens' behaviour and thereby encourage water conservation. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a weak argument based on irrelevance?

options.A: The policy should be adopted because it will reduce pollution
options.B: The policy should be adopted because the person proposing it has a pleasant voice
options.C: The policy should be adopted because it will improve public health
options.D: The policy should be adopted because it is feasible

questions.explanation: An argument is weak if it is irrelevant. The proposer's pleasant voice is irrelevant to the merits of the policy. A strong argument must address the issue directly.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'All the students who completed the assignment received a certificate. Meena received a certificate.' What can be inferred?

options.A: Meena completed the assignment
options.B: Meena may or may not have completed the assignment; receiving a certificate does not prove completion of the assignment
options.C: Meena did not complete the assignment
options.D: All students completed the assignment

questions.explanation: The passage states that all who completed the assignment received a certificate, but it does not state that only those who completed the assignment received certificates. Meena may have received a certificate for another reason. This is the fallacy of affirming the consequent.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following best describes a confounding factor?

options.A: A factor that directly causes the effect
options.B: A third variable that influences both variables being studied and can create or distort an apparent relationship between them
options.C: A factor that occurs after the effect
options.D: A factor that is unrelated to the study

questions.explanation: A confounding factor is a third variable that influences both variables being studied and can create or distort an apparent relationship between them.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the contrapositive of 'If a person is honest, then the person is respected'?

options.A: If a person is respected, then the person is honest
options.B: If a person is not respected, then the person is not honest
options.C: If a person is not honest, then the person is not respected
options.D: A person is honest and respected

questions.explanation: The contrapositive of 'If P then Q' is 'If not Q then not P'. Here: If a person is not respected, then the person is not honest. The contrapositive is logically equivalent to the original.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: No A is B. All C are B. Conclusion: No C is A. Does it follow?

options.A: Yes; C is inside B, and A has no overlap with B, so C has no overlap with A
options.B: No
options.C: Only if some C are A
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. All C are B, and no A is B. Therefore, no C can be A. This is a valid chain of reasoning.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The school should introduce a uniform dress code to improve discipline.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Uniforms are the only way to improve discipline
options.B: A uniform dress code can influence discipline and the school can implement it
options.C: Students dislike uniforms
options.D: Discipline is not important

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that a uniform dress code can influence discipline and that the school can implement it. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government increase taxes on sugary drinks? Argument: Yes, because higher prices may reduce consumption and improve public health. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides a significant health-related reason directly supporting the proposal
options.C: No, because people like sugary drinks
options.D: Yes, because all taxes are good

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects higher prices to reduced consumption and improved public health, both directly related to the proposal. It provides a reason supporting the action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The company has offices in five countries and employs over 1,000 people.' What can be inferred?

options.A: The company is large and operates internationally
options.B: The company is small
options.C: The company will expand to more countries
options.D: The company is not profitable

questions.explanation: Having offices in five countries and over 1,000 employees suggests the company is large and operates internationally. The other options are not supported by the passage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A new manager is appointed. Event II: Team performance improves. Which of the following would strengthen the claim that the manager caused the improvement?

options.A: The manager is popular
options.B: Performance improved only in the team led by the new manager, while similar teams without a new manager showed no improvement
options.C: The manager has many years of experience
options.D: The team likes the manager

questions.explanation: A comparison with similar teams that did not get a new manager helps establish causation by ruling out alternative explanations. This strengthens the claim that the new manager caused the improvement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the converse of 'If a number is divisible by 4, then it is even'?

options.A: If a number is even, then it is divisible by 4
options.B: If a number is not divisible by 4, then it is not even
options.C: If a number is not even, then it is not divisible by 4
options.D: A number is divisible by 4 and even

questions.explanation: The converse of 'If P then Q' is 'If Q then P'. Here: If a number is even, then it is divisible by 4. The converse is not generally equivalent to the original (e.g., 2 is even but not divisible by 4).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some B are C. Conclusion: Some A are C. Does it follow?

options.A: Yes, definitely
options.B: No; the B that is C may lie outside A
options.C: Yes, if all B are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. Some B are C, but the B that is C may lie outside A. 'All A are B' does not mean that the B's which are C are A. The overlap between B and C may be outside A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The company should provide training to its employees to improve productivity.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Training is the only way to improve productivity
options.B: Training can improve employees' skills and thereby increase productivity
options.C: Employees do not need training
options.D: All employees will benefit equally

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that training can improve employees' skills and thereby increase productivity. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the final exam approach, why should a candidate underline quantifiers and conditions?

options.A: To make the question look neat
options.B: To identify limiting words such as all, some, only, if, and unless that affect the logical structure of the question
options.C: To find the longest option
options.D: To guess the answer

questions.explanation: Underlining quantifiers and conditions helps identify limiting words such as all, some, only, if, and unless that affect the logical structure of the question. This is part of the final exam approach recommended in the notes.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between a premise and a conclusion?

options.A: They are the same
options.B: A premise is a statement accepted as the starting point for a logical argument; a conclusion is the result claimed to follow from one or more premises
options.C: A conclusion is the starting point, while a premise is the result
options.D: A premise is always false, while a conclusion is always true

questions.explanation: A premise is a statement or piece of information accepted as the starting point for a logical argument. A conclusion is the result claimed to follow from one or more premises.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'not' do to a proposition in logic?

options.A: It affirms the proposition
options.B: It reverses the truth value of the proposition
options.C: It makes the proposition neither true nor false
options.D: It combines two propositions

questions.explanation: Negation reverses the truth value of a proposition. If P is true, NOT P is false; if P is false, NOT P is true.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between a direct conclusion and an indirect conclusion?

options.A: They are the same
options.B: A direct conclusion follows immediately from a single statement or a straightforward combination; an indirect conclusion is reached by combining two or more premises through a chain of valid reasoning
options.C: An indirect conclusion follows immediately, while a direct conclusion requires a chain of reasoning
options.D: A direct conclusion is always false, while an indirect conclusion is always true

questions.explanation: A direct conclusion follows immediately from a single statement or a straightforward combination of the given statements. An indirect conclusion is reached by combining two or more premises through a chain of valid reasoning.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between an implicit assumption and an explicit assumption?

options.A: They are the same
options.B: An implicit assumption is not directly written but is required for the statement to make sense; an explicit assumption is stated openly
options.C: An explicit assumption is hidden, while an implicit assumption is stated openly
options.D: An implicit assumption is always false, while an explicit assumption is always true

questions.explanation: An implicit assumption is not directly written in the statement but is required or presupposed for the statement or argument to make sense. An explicit assumption is stated openly rather than left unstated.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between an argument from consequences and an argument from feasibility?

options.A: They are the same
options.B: An argument from consequences explains likely benefits, harms, costs, or wider effects; an argument from feasibility evaluates whether a proposal can practically be implemented
options.C: An argument from feasibility explains benefits, while an argument from consequences evaluates practicality
options.D: Both are based on moral principles

questions.explanation: An argument from consequences supports or opposes an action by explaining its likely benefits, harms, costs, or wider effects. An argument from feasibility evaluates whether a proposal can practically be implemented, considering resources, time, infrastructure, authority, and operational constraints.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between a direct inference and an indirect inference?

options.A: They are the same
options.B: A direct inference follows clearly from the given information with little or no intermediate reasoning; an indirect inference is obtained by connecting multiple pieces of information
options.C: An indirect inference follows clearly from one sentence, while a direct inference requires multiple connections
options.D: A direct inference is always uncertain, while an indirect inference is always certain

questions.explanation: A direct inference follows clearly from the given information with little or no intermediate reasoning. An indirect inference is obtained by connecting multiple pieces of information or identifying a relationship that is not stated in one sentence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between a direct cause and an indirect cause?

options.A: They are the same
options.B: A direct cause has an immediate causal connection with the effect; an indirect cause influences an outcome through one or more intermediate factors
options.C: An indirect cause has an immediate connection, while a direct cause involves intermediate factors
options.D: Both occur after the effect

questions.explanation: A direct cause has an immediate causal connection with the effect, without a substantial chain of intermediate events. An indirect cause influences an outcome through one or more intermediate factors.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between the converse and the contrapositive of a conditional?

options.A: They are the same
options.B: The converse is 'If Q then P' and is not generally equivalent to the original; the contrapositive is 'If not Q then not P' and is logically equivalent to the original
options.C: The contrapositive is not equivalent, while the converse is equivalent
options.D: Both are equivalent to the original

questions.explanation: The converse is 'If Q then P'. It is not generally equivalent and may be false even when the original conditional is true. The contrapositive is 'If not Q then not P'. It is logically equivalent to the original conditional.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: Some A are B. Some B are not C. Conclusion: Some A are not C. Does it follow?

options.A: No; the A that is B may be C, and the B that is not C may not be A
options.B: Yes, definitely
options.C: Only if all A are B
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. The A that is B may be C, and the B that is not C may not be A. The premises do not guarantee an overlap between A and the B's that are not C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The city should build more parks to improve residents' quality of life.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Parks are the only way to improve quality of life
options.B: Building more parks can contribute to improving residents' quality of life
options.C: Residents do not use parks
options.D: All cities have parks

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that building more parks can contribute to improving residents' quality of life. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government provide free laptops to students? Argument: Yes, because access to a laptop can help students study and complete assignments. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides a significant educational reason directly supporting the proposal
options.C: No, because laptops are expensive
options.D: Yes, because all students want laptops

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects access to a laptop to studying and completing assignments, both directly related to the proposal. It provides a reason supporting the action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The school's football team won all its matches this season.' What can be inferred?

options.A: The team did not lose any match this season
options.B: The team will win next season
options.C: The team is the best in the country
options.D: The team scored the most goals

questions.explanation: If the team won all its matches, it did not lose any match this season. The other options go beyond the passage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A person reads a book about nutrition. Event II: The person changes their diet. What is the relationship?

options.A: Reading about nutrition may have influenced the person's decision to change their diet
options.B: The diet change caused the person to read the book
options.C: The two events are unrelated
options.D: The diet change definitely and solely caused the reading

questions.explanation: Reading about nutrition may have influenced the person's decision to change their diet. However, other factors such as advice from a doctor or a friend could also have contributed.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the inverse of 'If a figure is a square, then it has four sides'?

options.A: If a figure has four sides, then it is a square
options.B: If a figure is not a square, then it does not have four sides
options.C: If a figure does not have four sides, then it is not a square
options.D: A figure is a square and has four sides

questions.explanation: The inverse of 'If P then Q' is 'If not P then not Q'. Here: If a figure is not a square, then it does not have four sides. The inverse is not generally equivalent to the original (e.g., a rectangle has four sides but is not a square).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some C are B. Conclusion: Some C are A. Does it follow?

options.A: No; the C that is B may not be A
options.B: Yes, definitely
options.C: Only if all C are B
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. Some C are B, but the C that is B may not be A. 'All A are B' does not mean 'All B are A'. The overlap between C and B may lie outside A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The government should improve public transportation to reduce traffic congestion.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Public transportation is the only solution to congestion
options.B: Improving public transportation can encourage more people to use it and thereby reduce traffic congestion
options.C: Traffic congestion is not a problem
options.D: All citizens will use public transportation

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that improving public transportation can encourage more people to use it and thereby reduce traffic congestion. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a circular argument?

options.A: The policy is effective because it works well
options.B: The policy is effective because data show it reduced unemployment
options.C: The policy is effective because it is feasible
options.D: The policy is effective because it is fair

questions.explanation: A circular argument uses the conclusion itself, or a restatement of it, as support. 'The policy is effective because it works well' restates the conclusion without independent evidence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The city has banned cars in the central area on Sundays.' What can be inferred about a Sunday in the central area?

options.A: Cars are not allowed in the central area
options.B: Cars are allowed in the central area
options.C: The central area is closed
options.D: The ban applies to all days

questions.explanation: If the city has banned cars in the central area on Sundays, then cars are not allowed in the central area on a Sunday. The inference follows directly from the passage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.A: The new restaurant may have drawn customers away from nearby restaurants
options.B: The decline in customers caused the new restaurant to open
options.C: The two events are unrelated
options.D: The decline in customers definitely and solely caused the new restaurant to open

questions.explanation: The new restaurant may have drawn customers away from nearby restaurants, which is a plausible direct causal relationship. However, other factors such as seasonal changes or road construction could also contribute.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the contrapositive of 'If a person is a doctor, then the person has a medical degree'?

options.A: If a person has a medical degree, then the person is a doctor
options.B: If a person does not have a medical degree, then the person is not a doctor
options.C: If a person is not a doctor, then the person does not have a medical degree
options.D: A person is a doctor and has a medical degree

questions.explanation: The contrapositive of 'If P then Q' is 'If not Q then not P'. Here: If a person does not have a medical degree, then the person is not a doctor. The contrapositive is logically equivalent to the original.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: No A is B. Some C are not B. Conclusion: Some C are not A. Does it follow?

options.A: No; the C that is not B may or may not be A
options.B: Yes, definitely
options.C: Only if all C are A
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The company should switch to renewable energy sources to reduce its carbon footprint.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.C: The company has no carbon footprint
options.D: All companies use renewable energy

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that switching to renewable energy sources can reduce the company's carbon footprint. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government impose a tax on junk food? Argument: Yes, because it would discourage consumption and improve public health. Is this argument strong?

options.C: No, because people enjoy junk food

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects the tax to reduced consumption and improved public health, both directly related to the proposal. It provides a reason supporting the action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The library has extended its opening hours from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays.' What can be inferred?

options.B: The library is open until 8 p.m. on weekdays

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A person starts meditating regularly. Event II: The person reports feeling less stressed. What is the most careful conclusion?

options.A: Meditation definitely caused the reduction in stress

options.C: The reduction in stress caused the meditation
options.D: The two events are unrelated

questions.explanation: Meditation may have contributed to the reduction in stress, but other factors such as lifestyle changes or social support could also explain it. Causation requires additional evidence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of 'Some A are not B'?

options.A: No A is B
options.B: At least one member of A is outside group B; it does not mean every member of A is outside B
options.C: All A are outside B
options.D: All B are A

questions.explanation: 'Some A are not B' means at least one member of A is outside group B. It does not mean that every member of A is outside B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. All B are C. No C is D. Conclusion: No A is D. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; A is inside B, B is inside C, and no C is D, so no A is D
options.C: Only if some A are D
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. All A are B, and all B are C, so all A are C. No C is D, so no A is D. The inclusion and exclusion relationships combine validly.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The school should organise more extracurricular activities to improve students' overall development.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Extracurricular activities are the only way to improve overall development
options.B: Extracurricular activities can contribute to students' overall development
options.C: Students do not need extracurricular activities
options.D: All students will participate

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that extracurricular activities can contribute to students' overall development. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a weak argument based on vagueness?

options.A: The policy should be adopted because it will reduce pollution by 20%
options.B: The policy should be adopted because it is good
options.C: The policy should be adopted because it is feasible
options.D: The policy should be adopted because it follows the principle of fairness

questions.explanation: A weak argument is vague or unsupported. 'It is good' is vague and does not provide a specific reason. A strong argument must be relevant, significant, logical, and adequately supported.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The company's profits declined in the last quarter, but its revenue increased.' What can be inferred?

options.A: The company's costs may have increased
options.B: The company is losing money
options.C: The company will go bankrupt
options.D: The company's revenue declined

questions.explanation: If revenue increased but profits declined, costs may have increased. This is a reasonable inference supported by the passage. The passage does not state that the company is losing money or will go bankrupt.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A person starts using a standing desk at work. Event II: The person reports less back pain. Which of the following would weaken the claim that the standing desk caused the reduction in back pain?

options.A: The person used the standing desk consistently
options.B: The person also started physiotherapy at the same time
options.C: The person found the standing desk comfortable
options.D: The standing desk was recommended by a doctor

questions.explanation: If the person also started physiotherapy at the same time, this is a confounding factor that could explain the reduction in back pain. It weakens the claim that the standing desk alone caused the improvement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct negation of 'All A are B'?

options.A: No A is B
options.B: Some A are not B
options.C: Some A are B
options.D: All A are not B

questions.explanation: The negation of 'All A are B' is 'Some A are not B'. These two statements are contradictory: they cannot both be true and cannot both be false.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: Some A are B. All A are C. Conclusion: Some C are B. Does it follow?

options.B: No; the A that is B may not be C
options.C: Only if all B are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some A are B. All A are C. The A that is B is also C. Therefore, some C are B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The government should invest in skill development programmes to reduce unemployment.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Skill development is the only way to reduce unemployment
options.B: Skill development programmes can improve employability and thereby reduce unemployment
options.C: Unemployment is not a problem
options.D: All unemployed people will join the programmes

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that skill development programmes can improve employability and thereby reduce unemployment. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government promote electric vehicles? Argument: Yes, because electric vehicles produce fewer emissions and help reduce air pollution. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides a significant environmental reason directly supporting the proposal
options.C: No, because electric vehicles are expensive
options.D: Yes, because everyone likes electric vehicles

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects electric vehicles to reduced emissions and air pollution, both directly related to the proposal. It provides a reason supporting the action.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'All the participants in the workshop were given certificates. Some participants were from other cities.' What can be inferred?

options.A: Some certificate recipients were from other cities
options.B: All certificate recipients were from other cities
options.C: No participant was from another city
options.D: The workshop was held in another city

questions.explanation: All participants received certificates, and some participants were from other cities. Therefore, some certificate recipients were from other cities. This is a valid inference.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of reverse causation?

options.A: Exercise reduces stress
options.B: People with lower stress levels may find it easier to exercise regularly
options.C: Stress and exercise are unrelated
options.D: Exercise always increases stress

questions.explanation: Reverse causation occurs when the assumed direction of cause and effect is reversed. It is possible that lower stress makes it easier to exercise, rather than exercise reducing stress.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of 'P only if Q'?

options.A: P is necessary for Q
options.B: Q is necessary for P; it is written as P → Q
options.C: Q is sufficient for P
options.D: P and Q are equivalent

questions.explanation: 'P only if Q' means that Q is necessary for P. It is written as P → Q. It does not mean that Q alone guarantees P.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. No B is C. Some C are D. Conclusion: Some D are not A. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; the D that is C cannot be B (since no B is C), and therefore cannot be A (since all A are B)
options.C: Only if all D are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some C are D. No B is C, so the C that is D cannot be B. All A are B, so anything that is not B cannot be A. Therefore, some D are not A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The city should introduce a bike-sharing scheme to reduce traffic congestion.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Bike-sharing is the only way to reduce congestion
options.B: A bike-sharing scheme can encourage people to cycle instead of driving and thereby reduce congestion
options.C: Traffic congestion is not a problem
options.D: All citizens own bicycles

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that a bike-sharing scheme can encourage people to cycle instead of driving and thereby reduce congestion. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the fallacy of affirming the consequent?

options.A: If it rains, the ground is wet. The ground is wet. Therefore, it rained.
options.B: If it rains, the ground is wet. It rained. Therefore, the ground is wet.
options.C: If it rains, the ground is wet. It did not rain. Therefore, the ground is not wet.
options.D: If it rains, the ground is wet. The ground is not wet. Therefore, it did not rain.

questions.explanation: The fallacy of affirming the consequent is: If P then Q; Q; therefore P. Option A follows this form. The ground may be wet for another reason (e.g., a water leak).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the fallacy of denying the antecedent?

options.A: If it rains, the ground is wet. The ground is wet. Therefore, it rained.
options.B: If it rains, the ground is wet. It did not rain. Therefore, the ground is not wet.
options.C: If it rains, the ground is wet. It rained. Therefore, the ground is wet.
options.D: If it rains, the ground is wet. The ground is not wet. Therefore, it did not rain.

questions.explanation: The fallacy of denying the antecedent is: If P then Q; not P; therefore not Q. Option B follows this form. The ground may still be wet for another reason even if it did not rain.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The school has 500 students, and 60% of them play at least one sport.' What can be inferred?

options.A: 300 students play at least one sport
options.B: 200 students play at least one sport
options.C: All students play sports
options.D: No student plays sports

questions.explanation: 60% of 500 students is 300. If 60% of the students play at least one sport, then 300 students play at least one sport. This is a direct inference.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.B: Employees reported liking the flexible hours
options.C: The company is in a competitive industry
options.D: The company has many employees

questions.explanation: If the company also introduced a pay rise at the same time, this is a confounding factor that could explain the increase in satisfaction. It weakens the claim that flexible working hours alone caused the improvement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of 'P if Q'?

options.A: P is necessary for Q
options.B: Q is sufficient for P; it is written as Q → P
options.C: Q is necessary for P
options.D: P and Q are equivalent

questions.explanation: 'P if Q' means that Q is sufficient for P. It is written as Q → P.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some B are C. No C is D. Conclusion: Some A are not D. Does it follow?

options.A: No; the B that is C may not include any A, and the D exclusion does not affect A
options.B: Yes, definitely
options.C: Only if all B are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. The B that is C may not include any A. The fact that no C is D does not affect A unless there is a guaranteed overlap between A and C, which is not established. Therefore, 'Some A are not D' does not necessarily follow.

options.C: Digital access is not important
options.D: All citizens have devices

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that providing free Wi-Fi in public places can improve digital access. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides significant safety and environmental reasons directly supporting the ban

options.D: Yes, because all bans are good

options.B: 'Wings of Fire' is not fiction
options.C: 'Wings of Fire' is not in the library
options.D: The library has no fiction books

questions.explanation: All books are either fiction or non-fiction. 'Wings of Fire' is non-fiction. Since the categories are mutually exclusive, it is not fiction. This is a valid inference.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.C: The student is a teenager
options.D: The student uses a smartphone

questions.explanation: If the student also started going to bed earlier at the same time, this is a confounding factor that could explain the improved sleep. It weakens the claim that reduced screen time alone caused the improvement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.A: P is necessary for Q, but Q is not necessary for P
options.B: P and Q imply each other; both are necessary and sufficient for one another
options.C: P and Q are unrelated
options.D: P is sufficient for Q, but Q is not sufficient for P

questions.explanation: 'P if and only if Q' means P and Q imply each other: P → Q and Q → P. Both are necessary and sufficient for one another.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: No A is B. All B are C. Conclusion: Some C are not A. Does it follow?

options.A: Yes; B is inside C, and no A is B, so the B that exists in C is not A
options.B: No; there may be no B
options.C: Only if all C are B
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. All B are C, so B is inside C. No A is B, so the B in C is not A. Therefore, some C are not A (assuming B exists, which is conventionally assumed in such problems unless stated otherwise).

questions.subject: Mental Ability

questions.explanation: The school requires all students to wear uniforms. Ravi is a student. Therefore, Ravi is required to wear a uniform. This is a direct inference.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.B: The difficulty in sleeping caused the person to eat a heavy meal
options.C: The two events are unrelated
options.D: The difficulty in sleeping definitely and solely caused the heavy meal

questions.explanation: Eating a heavy meal late at night may have contributed to the difficulty in sleeping. However, other factors such as stress or caffeine consumption could also explain it.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.A: 'All students passed' and 'Some students did not pass'
options.B: 'All students passed' and 'All students failed'
options.C: 'Some students passed' and 'Some students failed'
options.D: 'No student passed' and 'No student failed'

questions.explanation: 'All students passed' and 'Some students did not pass' are contradictory: they cannot both be true and cannot both be false. They are exact negations of each other.

questions.question: Statements: Some A are B. Some B are C. Conclusion: Some A are C. Does it follow?

options.A: No; the A-B overlap and the B-C overlap may involve different members of B
options.B: Yes, definitely
options.C: Only if all B are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: No. The A-B overlap and the B-C overlap may involve different members of B, so no overlap between A and C is guaranteed. Two 'some' premises do not yield a definite 'some' conclusion about A and C.

options.C: Vaccination is not important
options.D: All citizens are already vaccinated

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that a public awareness campaign can increase knowledge and thereby improve vaccination rates. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about weak arguments?
