options.B: A weak argument may be irrelevant, unsupported, vague, based on an incorrect assumption, emotionally manipulative, or insufficient to support the conclusion
options.C: A weak argument is always popular
options.D: A weak argument always uses statistics

questions.explanation: A weak argument is irrelevant, unsupported, vague, based on an incorrect assumption, emotionally manipulative, or insufficient to support the conclusion.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.A: If it rains, the match will be played
options.B: If it does not rain, the match will be played
options.C: If the match is played, it will rain
options.D: The match will not be played

questions.explanation: 'P unless Q' is commonly understood as 'if not Q, then P'. Here: If it does not rain, the match will be played. It can also be expressed as 'The match will be played or it will rain'.

options.B: No; the A that is C may not be B
options.C: Only if all C are A

options.A: Yes; the A that is B is also C, so some C are B
options.B: No; the A that is B may not be C
options.C: Only if all B are C
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. Some A are B. All A are C. The A that is B is also C. Therefore, some C are B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statement: 'The company should provide subsidised gym memberships to employees to promote a healthy lifestyle.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: Gym memberships are the only way to promote a healthy lifestyle
options.B: Subsidised gym memberships can encourage employees to exercise and promote a healthy lifestyle
options.C: Employees do not need exercise
options.D: All employees will use the gym

questions.explanation: The recommendation depends on the assumption that subsidised gym memberships can encourage employees to exercise and promote a healthy lifestyle. Without this, the recommendation would not make sense.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Question: Should the government impose a ban on single-use plastics? Argument: Yes, because single-use plastics are a major source of pollution and harm marine life. Is this argument strong?

options.A: No, because it is based on opinion
options.B: Yes; it is relevant and provides a significant environmental reason directly supporting the ban
options.C: No, because plastics are useful
options.D: Yes, because everyone supports the ban

questions.explanation: The argument is relevant and significant: it connects single-use plastics to pollution and harm to marine life, both directly related to the proposal. It provides a reason supporting the ban.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Passage: 'The school has 500 students, and 40% of them participate in sports.' What can be inferred?

options.A: 200 students participate in sports
options.B: 400 students participate in sports
options.C: All students participate in sports
options.D: No student participates in sports

questions.explanation: 40% of 500 is 200. If 40% of the students participate in sports, then 200 students participate in sports. This is a direct inference.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Event I: A company introduces a new software tool for project management. Event II: Project completion times decrease. Which of the following would strengthen the claim that the new software caused the decrease in completion times?

options.A: The software is easy to use
options.B: Project completion times decreased only after the software was introduced, and similar projects without the software showed no decrease
options.C: The company has many projects
options.D: The software is popular

questions.explanation: A comparison showing that project completion times decreased only after the software was introduced, while similar projects without the software showed no decrease, strengthens the causal claim by ruling out alternative explanations.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is a particular statement?

options.A: All applicants must carry an identity card
options.B: Every student passed the examination
options.C: Some teachers are writers
options.D: Each member must pay the fee

questions.explanation: A particular statement makes a claim about at least one or some members of a group. 'Some teachers are writers' is a particular statement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Statements: All A are B. Some C are not B. Conclusion: Some C are not A. Does it follow?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes; the C that is not B cannot be A, because all A are inside B
options.C: Only if some C are A
options.D: Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Yes. All A are B. Some C are not B. The C that lies outside B cannot be A, because every A is inside B. Therefore, some C are not A.

options.C: Chemical pollution is not a problem
options.D: All farmers will adopt organic farming

questions.subject: Mental Ability

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of 'If P, then Q'?

options.A: P is necessary for Q
options.B: P is sufficient for Q; Q is necessary for P
options.C: Q is sufficient for P
options.D: P and Q are equivalent

questions.explanation: 'If P, then Q' means that whenever P occurs, Q must follow. P is the sufficient condition and Q is the necessary condition.

options.D: Cannot be determined
